note: Assistant-authored generic->specific transformation pairs in Jeff's outlaw-country/Americana idiom. These teach the anti-cliche MOVE, not fixed phrasings. None are quoted from any existing song. cowriter.py renders a rotating subset (~6) into the {craft_examples} block for the draft and revise steps. 'Study the move, do not copy the words.'

transformations.generic: I'm so lonely now that you are gone
transformations.specific: Still set two cups out every mornin' / dump one down the drain
transformations.why: Trades a stated emotion for an observable habit that proves it

transformations.generic: I drove around in my old car all night
transformations.specific: Rolled the '92 down Route 7 'til the gas light come on
transformations.why: Exact make, road number, and a real consequence ground it in a real world

transformations.generic: My daddy's getting old and it makes me sad
transformations.specific: He asks about the weather twice / I answer twice, don't say a word about it
transformations.why: The decline and the son's grief are shown through behavior, never named

transformations.generic: Everything reminds me that our marriage fell apart
transformations.specific: The nursery's still that yellow we picked out / door stays shut now
transformations.why: Two images collide — hope and loss — with no line explaining the contrast

transformations.generic: I drowned my sorrows in a bottle of whiskey
transformations.specific: Poured the good bourbon out for the dog to smell / couldn't do it myself
transformations.why: Sidesteps the whiskey-drowning cliche for a stranger, truer image of restraint

transformations.generic: My heart is shattered into a million pieces tonight
transformations.specific: So that's it then. / Okay. / I'll get the boys on Sunday
transformations.why: Plainest possible words at the emotional peak hit harder than ornate ones

transformations.generic: The sad old screen door was hanging there
transformations.specific: Screen door slaps twice and settles / like it's got somethin' to say
transformations.why: A precise verb animates the image; the adjectives were doing nothing

transformations.generic: I still think about her all the time
transformations.specific: Her side of the truck still smells like drugstore vanilla
transformations.why: Smell fires memory harder than sight; the detail is oddly specific and true

transformations.generic: I've been sober for a year and it's been really hard
transformations.specific: Three hundred sixty-five days dry — / and not one of 'em I did for me
transformations.why: The second line turns the whole brag into something sadder and truer

transformations.generic: I got in my truck and then I drove to the river where we used to go and I sat there
transformations.specific: Keys. River. Same bend. / Sat 'til the frogs started up
transformations.why: Memory-style jump cuts trust the listener and move faster than connective tissue

transformations.generic: We just grew apart over time, you know how it goes
transformations.specific: It was the Tuesday you didn't laugh at the thing you always laugh at
transformations.why: The hyper-specific moment lets any listener map their own version onto it

transformations.generic: I'm from a small town by the river in the country
transformations.specific: Raised where the Ohio backs up in the bottoms every spring
transformations.why: Regional, place-specific phrasing beats the neutral national description
